title: Nigeria records $6.3bn in portfolio inflows this year as external reserves reach $55.6bn
body: Central Bank of Nigeria deputy governor Muhammad Sani Abdullahi said net foreign portfolio investment inflows reached $6.3bn between January and August 2026, strengthening dollar liquidity and reducing the need for direct FX intervention. Gross external reserves stood at $55.6bn as of 11 September, up from under $900m in net terms in 2023, with autonomous private sources now supplying nearly seven of every ten dollars entering the market in July.

title: Dangote breaks ground on $16bn East Africa refinery in Lamu, Kenya
body: Five African heads of state led the groundbreaking for the $16 billion Dangote East Africa Petroleum Refinery at Lamu, designed to process 700,000 barrels a day and complete in about 40 months. The complex is planned to include a 1,000MW power plant, one million tonnes of polypropylene capacity and base-oil production, anchoring the LAPSSET corridor. Kenya plans to take a stake via its National Infrastructure Fund and Dangote floated a Nairobi Securities Exchange offer for local ownership.

title: Zambia opens talks with IMF on new programme after $1.7bn arrangement expired
body: Zambia began discussions with a visiting IMF mission staying until 10 October, aiming to agree a new programme by year-end after its previous $1.7 billion arrangement expired in January. The country completed a sweeping debt restructuring and is seeking a second arrangement to consolidate it.

title: Burkina Faso's first gold refinery starts with 164-tonne annual capacity
body: Burkina Faso inaugurated its first gold refinery with initial capacity of 164 tonnes a year at a cost above 11 billion CFA francs, with plans to rise to 515 tonnes. President Traoré framed it as processing minerals locally and capturing more of the value chain at home.

title: Dangote pledges additional $50bn across Africa and wider public share offers
body: Speaking in Nairobi on the eve of the Lamu groundbreaking, Aliko Dangote said the Dangote Group would invest an additional $50 billion across Africa after more than $25 billion to date, and would progressively release more equity to African investors through capital markets to democratise industrial wealth.

title: Burkina Faso inaugurates its first-ever gold refinery as Traoré pledges local processing of minerals
body: Burkina Faso inaugurated its first gold refinery on 28 September, with President Ibrahim Traoré saying the state intends to process its mineral resources locally and control the value chain. The plant is small against the country's gold output but is the Sahel's most concrete step yet toward the economic-sovereignty doctrine of refining at home rather than exporting raw ore.

title: South Africa's FDI inflows more than doubled in Q2 to R49.8bn
body: South Africa's foreign direct investment inflows rose to 49.8 billion rand in the second quarter, up from 20.3 billion rand in the first, even as the rand weakened on higher oil prices. The rebound lands amid continued industrial investment interest despite grid and logistics constraints.

title: Rwanda and China launch a $47 million irrigation project
body: Rwanda and China launched a 47-million-USD irrigation project, adding to the growing slate of Chinese-financed agricultural infrastructure on the continent, alongside renewed pushes for China-Africa textile cooperation and deeper Egypt-Ghana business ties with Chinese partners.

title: Ghana seeks direct currency settlement for trade with China
body: Ghanaian authorities said they will work with their Chinese counterparts to eliminate third-party currency settlements in bilateral trade, moving toward direct cedi-renminbi settlement — part of a broader African shift toward local-currency trade finance.

title: Rwanda receives first 40,000-tonne government-backed fuel cargo through Kenya's Mombasa corridor
body: The 40,000-metric-tonne cargo aboard MT Sea Wolf berthed at Kenya Pipeline Company's Kipevu Oil Terminal 2 in Mombasa, operationalising the Rwanda-Kenya fuel import framework signed on June 29, 2026. Under the agreements, Rwanda can independently source bulk refined products while using Kenya's port, pipeline and storage infrastructure along the Northern Corridor, with imports projected to rise from roughly 42,000-50,000 cubic metres in 2025 to more than 500,000 cubic metres annually. Kenya also extended storage rights for Rwanda-bound fuel from 35 to up to 90 days, letting Kigali build strategic stocks alongside its existing Tanzania corridors.

title: South Africa and Mozambique move to ease Lebombo border gridlock as truck volumes exceed 1,800 a day
body: South Africa's Border Management Authority and SARS, working with Mozambican officials deployed to the KM7 staging facility, are processing more than 1,600 trucks a day at the Lebombo Port of Entry, with peak volumes topping 1,800. Authorities have installed ANPR cameras, boom gates and scanning infrastructure, while longer-term plans include a One-Stop Border Post, port redevelopment and expanded rail capacity to take pressure off the road corridor that carries much of South Africa-Mozambique trade.

title: Dangote Lagos refinery IPO draws 'enormous' demand, Dangote says
body: Aliko Dangote said the $1.6bn IPO of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery — marketed as Africa's largest 'people's IPO' to fund doubling capacity toward 1.4 million bpd — has attracted 'enormous' investor demand, though he gave no subscription figures. The remarks were made in Nairobi ahead of the Lamu East African refinery groundbreaking.

title: Nigeria closes oversubscribed N728.9bn Series 2 power-sector bond, taking the debt-clearing programme to about N1.23tn
body: NBET Finance Company's Series 2 bond, structured with Africa Finance Corporation as co-financial adviser under the Presidential Power Sector Financial Reforms Programme, closed oversubscribed with demand from pension funds, banks and asset managers to settle legacy electricity-sector debts. Cumulative issuance under the programme now stands at roughly N1.23tn, after the N501bn Series 1 closed in January 2026.

title: Nigeria faces crude supply crunch as refinery demand nears 1.5m bpd against 1.68m bpd output
body: IPPG chairman Adegbite Falade warned at the 2026 Nigeria Oil Refining Summit in Lagos that domestic refineries could require more than 1.5 million barrels per day in the medium term, close to Nigeria's 1.68 million bpd liquids output in August per NUPRC, leaving a narrow margin for exports, government revenue and OPEC commitments. NUPRC said refiners transacted 112 million of the 182 million barrels offered to them between January and August. Refiners also pressed for an overhaul of the naira-for-crude scheme and a domestic crude pricing template.

title: Sweden invites Nigeria to submit priority projects for financing, guarantees and investment support
body: Swedish ambassador Anna Westerholm invited Nigeria to submit priority development project proposals after a meeting with the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning in Abuja, with proposals routed through the Swedish Embassy or Business Sweden's trade commissioner. Potential cooperation areas include digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence, data centres, energy, transport, agriculture and tourism. Budget Minister Abubakar Bagudu pointed to the proposed National Development Finance Corporation as a mechanism for structuring bankable projects.

title: Benin mobilises €500m in international financing backed by African Development Fund guarantee
body: Benin secured €500 million (about CFAF 328 billion) in 12-year international bank financing for education, health, water access, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture and youth and women's employment. The transaction, completed 18 September, is the second AfDF-supported deal since 2023 and uses a partial credit guarantee from the African Development Fund plus second-loss insurance from the Islamic Development Bank Group's insurance subsidiary to borrow on competitive terms.

title: Dangote breaks ground on $16 billion, 700,000 bpd refinery at Lamu, Kenya
body: Aliko Dangote confirmed the $16 billion East African refinery at Lamu will break ground this week, with planned capacity of 700,000 barrels per day, a 30% stake offered to regional governments including Kenya and Rwanda, and about 60,000 jobs expected. East African governments' equity payments may be spread over four years, and pipelines into neighbouring countries are planned. He told AFP the project is part of a push for Africa to be largely self-sufficient in refined fuel by 2030.

title: AfCFTA Secretariat partners with All Africa IP Summit to turn brands and creativity into trade assets
body: The AfCFTA Secretariat and the All Africa Intellectual Property Summit have entered a strategic partnership to build a common continental intellectual property framework alongside AfCFTA, helping businesses and creators protect brands and inventions and derive commercial value from them. Secretary-General Wamkele Mene said the adoption of the eight Annexes creates a framework that supports African innovation and the creative economy.
source: The High Street Journal via tralac

title: Central African states advance regional energy information system for investment planning
body: Energy ministers from the six CEMAC member states met in Libreville, Gabon, on September 25 to advance plans for a CEMAC Energy Information System aimed at improving policymaking, investment planning and cooperation across the region's energy sector. The meeting capped a week of technical work with CEMAC, the African Energy Commission and the World Bank, whose support flows through its Statistics Harmonisation and Improvement Project for West and Central Africa.

title: Egypt prepares FDI strategy spanning 1,330 opportunities across 16 sectors
body: Egypt's investment and foreign trade minister said the country is preparing to unveil a foreign direct investment strategy that includes 1,330 investment opportunities covering 16 industrial sectors, aimed at boosting non-oil exports and maximising hard currency earnings.

title: Nigeria DRE Fund, $300m solar minigrid vehicle co-managed by NSIA and Africa50, moves into active deployment after commercial launch
body: The $300 million Nigeria Distributed Renewable Energy (DRE) Fund reached its commercial launch during Unstoppable Africa 2026 in New York, marking the shift from fund structuring to active capital deployment. Co-managed by the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) and Africa50 with SEforALL and World Bank support, it provides equity to local clean-energy developers for solar mini-grids, solar home systems, commercial and industrial power and storage, aligned with Mission 300's target of connecting 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030.

title: Kenya manufacturers push AfCFTA from signatures to delivery at Unstoppable Africa 2026
body: Kenya Association of Manufacturers vice chair Mary-Ann Musangi told the Unstoppable Africa 2026 forum in New York that Africa has moved beyond negotiating AfCFTA and must now make the framework deliver for businesses, with the private sector in the driver's seat. She argued tariff cuts alone do not create viable trade: border delays, repeated inspections, inconsistent documentation and costly certification remain the practical barriers, so standards convergence and simpler cross-border processes are the priorities. The session, 'Tools and Architects: Putting Africa's Private Sector in the AfCFTA Driver's Seat', ran on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.

title: Burkina Faso opens its first gold refinery, RAFFINOR-BF, to refine gold at home
body: President Ibrahim Traoré inaugurated Burkina Faso's first gold refinery, RAFFINOR-BF, in Ouagadougou on September 28. Financed by the state via SONASP with private partners at a cost of 11 billion CFA francs, it can process 164 tonnes of gold annually, rising to 515 tonnes in a second phase. Gold was nearly 94% of the country's export earnings in the first seven months of 2026, and until now most of it left as unrefined doré.

title: Africa's disinflation broadens but oil above $100 threatens the gains
body: Nine of 16 African economies tracked recorded lower annual inflation in August, extending the continent's disinflation trend, with Mozambique, Côte d'Ivoire and Angola falling the most. The improvement predates Brent crude's climb above $100 since early September on Middle East tensions, which is already pushing Nigerian petrol to about N1,400 per litre. Central banks face a test: Nigeria cut its rate by 350bp to 23% in September, its biggest reduction since 2007, while South Africa's reserve bank raised 25bp to 7.25% on September 23 citing upside risks.

title: Dangote Cement plans ~45% capacity expansion, funded mainly from operating cash flow
body: Dangote Cement is planning to add about 25 million tonnes of annual capacity to its stated 55-million-tonne base - roughly 45% growth - with management describing operating cash flow and supplier credit as the primary funding sources rather than new borrowing. Group MD/CEO Arvind Pathak outlined the strategy at the September 21 Capital Markets Day in London, with planned additions in Cameroon and Senegal; Kenya is excluded because no limestone deposit meeting the group requirements for size, quality and proximity has been identified. The plan sits inside Dangote Group's $45 billion investment program and a $100 billion annual revenue ambition by 2030; Dangote Cement reported turnover of $3.1 billion for the twelve months to June, up 22%.

title: Burkina Faso inaugurates its first gold refinery, Raffinor BF, to refine gold domestically
body: Burkina Faso is inaugurating its first gold refinery, Raffinor BF, in Ouagadougou, with a processing capacity of up to 400 kilograms of gold per day on a five-hectare site including a foundry and analysis laboratory. The facility, whose foundation stone was laid by President Ibrahim Traoré in November 2023, is meant to keep more of the country's gold — historically refined abroad — processed and monetized domestically. It is a flagship piece of the government's push to raise state presence in mining and capture more value from extracted resources.

title: Gold Fields eyes takeover of Australia's biggest gold miner Northern Star
body: Johannesburg-listed Gold Fields has approached Australia's Northern Star Resources about a potential takeover, per people familiar with the matter, though Northern Star rebuffed the overtures. A deal would deepen the South African gold major's bet on Australian deposits and extend a wave of gold-sector dealmaking driven by record prices; Gold Fields is valued around $35.7 billion versus Northern Star's $31.5 billion after a 17% share slide this year.

title: Kenya to break ground on Dangote-backed $16bn East African oil refinery at Lamu
body: Kenya will on 30 September break ground on the East African Oil Refinery at Lamu Port, a $16bn joint project with Nigeria Dangote Group designed for up to 700,000 barrels per day. The facility, the largest industrial investment in East Africa, is expected to supply fuel to Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan and Ethiopia, and to spur petrochemical and fertiliser industries along the LAPSSET corridor.

title: Dangote and Ethiopia launch $660m Ethiopia-Djibouti petroleum pipeline
body: Aliko Dangote has announced a $660m fuel pipeline linking Djibouti Damerjog port to Dewele in Ethiopia, with about 400 million litres of storage, expected to begin operations within 18 months. Landlocked Ethiopia relies heavily on Djibouti for imports, and the pipeline is expected to cut fuel transport time to Addis Ababa from five days to one.

title: US and China compete over Ethiopia $12.5bn Bishoftu International Airport
body: Ethiopia $12.5bn four-runway Bishoftu International Airport has drawn construction bids from Chinese-led consortiums and technology and financing interest from the US, with the African Development Bank mandated to raise up to $8bn in debt. The airport, due to open in 2030 with initial capacity of 60 million passengers a year, would become one of Africa biggest aviation hubs and serve the fast-growing Ethiopian Airlines Group.

title: Agriculture Summit Africa: continent pushes new agri-finance model and local processing
body: At the ninth Agriculture Summit Africa, delegates agreed Africa must move beyond exporting raw commodities to owning the processing, storage, trade and finance that capture value at home. Agriculture Minister Abubakar Kyari noted Africa spends more than $100 billion a year importing food it can produce itself. Sterling Bank executives argued food security is now a national security question and that finance must be redesigned for agriculture's long cycles, including livestock lending.

title: Kenya in advanced talks with US on critical minerals processing deal
body: Kenya mining minister Hassan Ali Joho says talks with the US government on a deal to develop Kenya critical minerals processing industry are at a very advanced stage, covering refineries and processing plants that would partly supply the US market. Discussions involve the US departments of commerce, defense and state and are intertwined with the bidding process for Mrima Hill, a coastal deposit expected to hold tens of billions of dollars worth of rare earths. Kenya mining currently contributes about 1% of GDP and the government targets 10% within a decade.

title: Dangote Group targets $36bn 2026 revenue, plans to double Nigerian refinery capacity
body: Dangote Group chief strategy officer Aliyu Suleiman says the conglomerate generated about $17 billion in first-half 2026 revenue and is on course to reach $36 billion for the full year, roughly double its 2025 total of $18 billion. The disclosure came during Kenyan President William Ruto tour of the 700,000-barrel-per-day Lekki refinery ahead of the September 30 Lamu groundbreaking. Dangote also plans to lift the Nigerian refinery to about 1.4 million barrels per day via a new 750,000-barrel-per-day crude distillation unit.

title: Nigeria woos German industrial investors toward its $1 trillion economy target
body: Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Abubakar Atiku Bagudu called on German companies to invest more actively in Nigeria industrial sector, saying the $1 trillion economy target for 2030 cannot be met without stronger private-sector production and investment in manufacturing, mining, construction and infrastructure. A German-Nigerian Industrial Technology Conference discussed technology transfer and financing options, including a 300 million euro German export credit guarantee scheme. The NESG urged moving beyond stabilisation reforms into productive investment.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO tops MTN and GTCO digital subscription records in its first day
body: The ongoing Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO surpassed in its first day the digital subscription levels of Nigeria's previous landmark offers - GTCO's (about 150,000 digital investors) and MTN Nigeria's (120,000-130,000 subscribers) - according to Chapel Hill Denham, a co-arranger of the deal. The offer of 4.1 billion new shares at N525 each, which opened 14 September and closes 13 October, seeks to raise about N2.15 trillion - one of the largest equity raises ever undertaken in Africa - with an ambition of reaching 10 million investors, benchmarked against Saudi Aramco's roughly 4.9-million-investor IPO.

title: COCOBOD turns to domestic investors as Cocoa Capital opens bookbuild under GH¢16.3bn cocoa notes programme
body: Cocoa Capital PLC, a special-purpose vehicle owned by the Ghana Cocoa Board, opened its bookbuild on 28 September for the first issue under a Domestic Cocoa Notes Programme of up to GH¢16.3 billion (about $1.4 billion), after the collapse of COCOBOD’s decades-old syndicated offshore loan. The 270-day cedi commercial paper, listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange and repaid in June 2027, funds seasonal cocoa purchases alongside a planned GH¢2.3 billion bond to refinance legacy debt, with repayments backed by assigned cocoa export receivables. Licensed buyers say COCOBOD still owes them about GH¢4 billion for last season, and the board expects 2026/27 production to fall at least 16%.

title: First machinery for Dangote-backed $16bn Lamu refinery docks at Lamu Port ahead of September 30 groundbreaking
body: The vessel MV Da Yang docked at Lamu Port carrying about 2,930 tonnes of construction equipment from China — the first cargo for the $16 billion, 700,000-barrel-per-day Dangote East Africa Refinery, which President William Ruto is expected to break ground on Wednesday, September 30. The project, backed by Aliko Dangote and the Africa Finance Corporation within the LAPSSET corridor, is targeted for completion by 2030 and projected to create about 60,000 jobs; Kenya Ports Authority expects a steady stream of crude and product tankers to lift port traffic and revenue.

title: Burstone and Nedbank launch R5.4bn South African funds management platform
body: Johannesburg-listed Burstone has agreed to seed a new unlisted funds management platform with 14 South African retail and industrial properties (gross asset value about R5.4 billion, blended yield 8.4%), selling 50% to Nedbank Property Partners for about R677 million (about $41.6 million). Burstone keeps half the equity and acts as fund and asset manager, releasing about R4.5 billion of capital; the deal, announced on 25 September and subject to Competition Commission approval, is expected to take effect by 1 December, with a second close under discussion with an institutional investor.

title: Three mega-projects put $40bn behind East Africa’s Indian Ocean trade ambitions
body: Business Insider Africa counts more than $40 billion behind three projects reshaping East Africa’s Indian Ocean coast: Dangote’s proposed $17 billion refinery and petrochemical complex at Lamu, Kenya; a nearly $4 billion Turkish-backed port, special economic zone and industrial hub near Warsheekh, Somalia, confirmed by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre with highway construction already underway toward Mogadishu; and a $20 billion-plus energy hub at Tanga, Tanzania, being developed with Uganda under a UNOC, TPDC and Vitol Bahrain MoU to complement the EACOP crude pipeline and Uganda’s planned Hoima refinery.

title: AfDB mobilises $4.1bn for countries hit by energy and fertiliser price shocks
body: The African Development Bank said its Global Energy And Fertilizer Crisis Response Framework has mobilised $4.1 billion in financing, plus an additional $960 million in concessional funding, for countries hit by global energy, food and fertiliser price shocks driven mainly by the Middle East conflicts. Directors noted African economies remain heavily import-dependent on those commodities.

title: Dangote unveils Vision 2030: $115bn turnover, $35bn annual profit, $8bn LNG plant
body: The Dangote Group detailed its Vision 2030, targeting over $115 billion in group turnover and $35 billion in annual profit by 2030, anchored on nearly $50 billion in new investments across Africa. The plan includes an $8 billion, 13-metric-tonnes-per-annum LNG plant and the $16bn East Africa refinery in Lamu, Kenya, which breaks ground on September 30.

title: Refinery closures leave South Africa more exposed to imported fuel shocks
body: New South African Reserve Bank research estimates the oil-import bill could have been R76 billion lower between 2021 and 2024 if refined products had stayed at no more than 25 percent of total oil imports. Imported refined products now supply more than half of domestic fuel demand as local refining capacity has declined, economists warned.

title: Only 26 African states have gazetted AfCFTA tariff schedules, Secretariat says
body: The AfCFTA Secretariat says only 26 African countries have gazetted the tariff schedules exporters need to claim lower cross-border duties, up from 25 in March 2026, though 48 of 50 submitted offers have been finalised. Joyce Letswalo, head of the Secretariat Market Access Division, said gazetting is the step that matters to businesses: an exporter can claim the AfCFTA rate only once the importing country has published its schedule nationally and loaded it into its customs system. Non-least-developed members have now removed duties on the 90 percent of tariff lines covered by provisional schedules; talks continue on the 7 percent sensitive and 3 percent excluded lines.

title: Kenya breaks ground on $16bn Dangote-led Lamu refinery, larger than the Lagos plant
body: Kenya will break ground on September 30 for the East African Oil Refinery at Lamu port, a $16 billion, 700,000-barrel-per-day project developed with Aliko Dangote and billed as bigger than his Lagos refinery, paired with a 1,000 MW power plant. President Ruto says land is secured and approvals are being fast-tracked; the plant is meant to supply fuel across East Africa and cut refined-product imports.

title: Northern Star rejects Gold Fields's $27.2bn takeover bid
body: Northern Star's board unanimously rejected Gold Fields' unsolicited US$27.2bn (A$38.7bn) cash-and-stock proposal, calling it opportunistic and saying it materially undervalued the Australian miner; the tie-up would have created the world's second-largest gold producer with about 4.1Moz of annual output and $4-5bn in estimated synergies. Gold Fields says it remains open to constructive dialogue, while activist Elliott Investment Management keeps pressing Northern Star for strategic options.

title: CBN cuts Monetary Policy Rate to 23% in 350bps move, holds cash reserve ratio at 45%
body: Nigeria's central bank cut its benchmark Monetary Policy Rate from 26.5% to 23% — a 350-basis-point reduction and one of its biggest monetary-policy shifts in recent years. The Monetary Policy Committee kept the cash reserve ratio for banks at 45% and recalibrated the standing facilities corridor to +50/-300 basis points around the new rate. T-bill and FGN bond yields had already fallen sharply ahead of the decision, and analysts caution that cheaper bank lending will depend on how quickly the cut passes through.

title: Ghana to sign deal for 1,200MW state-owned gas power plant by end of 2026, its biggest ever
body: President John Mahama said Ghana will sign an agreement before the end of 2026 for a 1,200MW state-owned gas-fired power plant, which would surpass the 1,020MW Akosombo hydro station as the country's largest single generating facility. He said the project will be financed entirely from Ghana's own resources without new borrowing, drawing on additional gas from the Offshore Cape Three Points and Jubilee fields and Ghana Gas' second processing plant. The plant is part of the government's 'Big Push' agenda to reduce reliance on independent power producers.

title: Dangote, Turkish investors and East African states back $40bn of Indian Ocean trade megaprojects
body: Three projects worth over $40 billion are reshaping East Africa's Indian Ocean coast: a $17bn Dangote-backed refinery and petrochemical complex at Lamu, Kenya; a $20bn-plus Tanzania-Uganda energy hub at Tanga (UNOC, TPDC and Vitol MoU) with refining, pipelines and storage; and a near-$4bn Turkish-backed port, special economic zone and industrial hub near Warsheekh, Somalia. Together they position the coastline as an integrated gateway for landlocked economies from Ethiopia to DR Congo.

title: Capital Economics: sub-Saharan Africa growth to hit 4.1% this year, Nigeria heading for 5%
body: Capital Economics quarterly outlook sees sub-Saharan Africa growth picking up to 4.1% in 2026 from 3.6% in 2025, with oil and metal exporters (Nigeria, Angola, Ghana, Zambia) weathering the energy shock while Kenya, Ethiopia and Mozambique face rate hikes and currency pressure. Nigeria is the standout call: 4.5% this year and 5% by 2027, its strongest run since the 2000s.

title: AfCFTA Secretariat and All Africa IP Summit partner to turn African ideas and brands into trade assets
body: The AfCFTA Secretariat and the All Africa Intellectual Property Summit have formed a strategic partnership to strengthen the role of intellectual property in intra-African trade, industrialisation, innovation and the creative economy. It builds on the African Union approval in February 2026 of eight of the nine Annexes under the AfCFTA Protocol on Intellectual Property Rights, covering patents, marks, industrial designs, copyright, traditional knowledge and related rights. The partnership will support the 7th All Africa Intellectual Property Summit in Nairobi on November 11-13, 2026, where delegates are expected to adopt the Nairobi Declaration on intellectual property and economic transformation.

title: Nigeria moves to tighten Special Economic Zone rules, recognising Digital Free Zones for the first time
body: The Federal Government Special Economic Zones Legislative and Regulatory Reform Committee began a drafting retreat to convert ongoing consultations into revised legislative and regulatory instruments. Industry, Trade and Investment Minister Jumoke Oduwole said existing incentives - duty-free importation of capital goods, tax exemption on qualifying export profits, 100 percent foreign ownership and unrestricted capital repatriation - will be preserved, while new measures curb diversion of Free Zone goods into the domestic market under a proposed 75/25 export-domestic sales framework. Draft regulations recognise Digital Free Zones and Digital Free Zone Enterprises for the first time, following a presidential directive with a 180-day roadmap to full launch.

title: Research: AfCFTA lifted African firms international-sales intensity by about 2.7 percentage points by 2022
body: Economists affiliated with the University of York, Queen Mary University of London, the IMF and Miami University, analysing 18,094 firm-year observations across 1,244 firms in 27 African economies, find that the ratio of international sales to total sales rose about 1 percentage point after the 2018 AfCFTA signing, reaching roughly 2.7 percentage points by 2022. Gains were concentrated among firms with prior export experience, which gained about 3.4 percentage points more than firms without it, and among firms able to finance production expansion. The authors argue market access alone will not deliver broad-based gains without trade finance, infrastructure, digital customs systems and export-readiness support.

title: UN launches Global Grids Accelerator to speed grid investment in Africa
body: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres launched the Global Grids Accelerator ahead of the UN Climate Summit 2026, aiming to turn government grid priorities into investable projects across Africa and South-East Asia. In Africa it will build on the Continental Power System Master Plan, the African Single Electricity Market, PIDA and Mission 300, working with the AU Commission, the AfDB and other development banks. AfDB President Sidi Ould Tah said it would reinforce Mission 300s goal of connecting 300 million more people to electricity by 2030.

title: Nigeria backs flared-gas power project for 80,000 Niger Delta connections
body: Clean-energy firm Energy Ventures B.V. has secured Federal Government backing to harness flared gas in the Niger Delta to supply electricity to about 80,000 homes and businesses, roughly half a million people. The project, which has already piloted at the Abada oil field, could serve as a template to unlock energy from over 100 other flare sites across Nigeria while cutting pollution from decades of gas flaring.

title: Afreximbank and ATDC sign $500m global credit facility to scale African trade and distribution
body: Afreximbank and the Africa Trading and Distribution Company (ATDC) signed a $500 million Global Credit Facility to finance the aggregation, logistics, warehousing and distribution of African-made goods across the continent, supporting AfCFTA implementation. ATDC, a pan-African trading platform with operations in Egypt, Nigeria, Malawi and Zimbabwe, will use the facility to strengthen supply chains, deepen regional value chains and expand market access for African manufacturers.

title: Nigeria power reset: grid output tops 5,000MW as minister lays out transmission super grid plan
body: Nigeria’s Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe, marking his first 100 days, reported generation and transmission above 5,000MW (peaking at 5,330MW) versus 3,700–4,700MW before June, with the 375MW Alaoji plant back online and new transformers unlocking over 900MW of transmission capacity. The blueprint includes a Transmission Super Grid with audits on the Lagos and Abuja corridors, dedicated power for industrial clusters, state-level decentralised markets under the Electricity Act 2023, and 62 solar/mini-grid installations across 30 states.

title: BB Energy launches merchant power trading business in SADC, co-developing merchant solar plant in Namibia
body: BB Energy Group has established a new Power Trading business, aiming to become one of the first merchant players trading on the Southern African Power Pool markets. Its renewables arm Solarcentury Africa has signed a Joint Development Agreement to co-develop a solar plant in Namibia designed to sell power directly to large industrial and mining customers and to export through the SAPP network.

title: Uganda locks in 121 million dollars from African Development Fund for South Sudan power interconnection
body: Uganda has secured about 121 million US dollars from the African Development Fund for its component of the South Sudan-Uganda Power Interconnection Project, with a technical launch held by the energy and finance ministries, UETCL and the AfDB. The interconnection will reinforce Ugandas northern grid, give diesel-dependent South Sudan access to cheaper electricity, and open an export revenue stream for Ugandas surplus power.

title: Kenya's first commercial oil gears up: KSh2bn-plus rig lands in Mombasa ahead of November drilling
body: A 1,500-horsepower GW70 drilling rig, part of a 2,152-tonne consignment that arrived aboard MV Transit Sedanka, has docked at the Port of Mombasa for the South Lokichar Basin development in Turkana. Operator Gulf Energy E&P, which bought the assets from Tullow in 2025, plans to begin drilling on November 1 and targets Kenya's first commercial crude production in December 2026, with first exports through Mombasa expected in the first quarter of 2027. The wider project is estimated at about $6 billion, with phase one targeting 20,000 barrels per day, rising to 50,000 in a second phase.

title: Nigeria takes 'Hire From Nigeria' global, targeting one million export-linked jobs by 2030
body: Vice President Kashim Shettima declared Nigeria 'the next frontier for global outsourcing' at the global launch of the Hire From Nigeria campaign in New York, held on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The private-sector-led, government-backed campaign connects Nigerian professionals, digital experts, creatives and service providers with global employers, with an initial target of one million export-linked jobs by 2030. The New York launch followed the national launch in Abuja on August 31.

title: Six CEMAC states back a shared regional energy data system (SIE-CEMAC)
body: Energy ministers from six Central African states, meeting in Libreville on September 25, approved a draft regulation creating the Community Energy Information System (SIE-CEMAC) and a roadmap to harmonise how energy data is collected and published across the bloc. The move tackles weak, non-comparable national statistics in a region with only about 3,700 MW of installed capacity and household electricity access as low as 13% in Chad. The texts now go to the CEMAC Council of Ministers for adoption, and the system is intended to feed the African Union's AFREC continental energy database.

title: Luno acquires Kenyan cross-border payments firm GTXN
body: Crypto platform Luno has acquired GTXN, a Kenyan cross-border payments company, bringing licensed collection and payout infrastructure in-house as it expands into business payments across emerging markets. GTXN will operate as Luno's cross-border payments capability, with transactions running on Luno's payment rails and settling against its liquidity. Financial terms were not disclosed; GTXN co-founder Dan Kleinbaum stays on as chief executive.

title: USTDA funds feasibility study to expand hydropower along the Lobito Corridor
body: The U.S. Trade and Development Agency signed an agreement with Anzana Electric Group during UN General Assembly High-Level Week to fund a feasibility study expanding hydropower generation and upgrading electricity distribution across Lualaba Province in the DRC and Zambia's North-Western Province. The project aims to improve power reliability for copper and cobalt mining operations and more than three million residents along the strategic Lobito Corridor logistics route.

title: Mercuria enters African power market with $250 million Zambia investment
body: Global energy and commodities trader Mercuria and Africa-focused investor Exergy have signed a $250 million financing agreement supporting electricity generation and transmission projects across Southern and Eastern Africa. The investment, one of the largest private-capital commitments to Zambia's power sector, will finance Exergy subsidiaries Lunzua Power, Lusitu Transmission and Distribution and Kanona, including a transmission highway to improve Zambia's connection with East African electricity markets. Zambia is targeting about 10,000 MW of electricity supply by 2031.

title: Nigeria closes N729 billion Series 2 power sector bond as reform programme hits N1.23 trillion
body: Africa Finance Corporation served as Co-Financial Adviser on the successful close of NBET Finance Company Plc's N728.9 billion Series 2 power sector bond under Nigeria's Presidential Power Sector Financial Reforms Programme. The oversubscribed issuance, following a N501 billion Series 1 in January 2026, brings cumulative issuance to about N1.23 trillion, with proceeds settling verified legacy receivables owed to generation companies and impacting approximately 5,398 MW of generation capacity.

title: IFC considers $8.6 million debt for 14 solar mini-grids across four Nigerian states
body: The International Finance Corporation is considering up to $8.6 million in debt financing for Nigerian renewable energy company Nayo Tropical Technology to build 14 solar mini-grids totalling 14 MW in Enugu, the Federal Capital Territory, Ondo and Niger states. The $29.7 million projects fall under IFC's $200 million DARES platform, which provides debt to mini-grid developers and is expected to expand electricity access where supply is unreliable.

title: Kenya and Italy line up $419 million partnership for 15 new hospitals under the Mattei Plan
body: Kenya President William Ruto, addressing the ECAM Council Summit at UNGA 81, highlighted a $419 million healthcare partnership with Italy and GKSD Group (Gruppo San Donato) signed on 8 September as a letter of intent to build 15 hospitals across 15 counties - 13 Level 5 county referral hospitals and two Level 6 national teaching and referral facilities. The deal is part of Italy’s Mattei Plan for Africa, with financing structuring, design and procurement still to follow. Ruto framed it as an example of the shift from aid dependence toward investment and technology-transfer partnerships in Africa.

title: Kenya boosts stake in Africa Finance Corporation by KSh3.25 billion
body: President William Ruto announced Kenya has increased its shareholding in the pan-African infrastructure financier Africa Finance Corporation by $25 million (KSh3.25 billion), following a visit to AFC's Lagos headquarters. The move deepens Kenya's push to channel domestic capital into African financial institutions and infrastructure, and comes as Ruto courts AFC involvement in the planned Lamu refinery.

title: Kenya to break ground on Dangote East African Refinery in Lamu next week
body: President William Ruto, speaking during a visit to the Dangote refinery in Lekki, Lagos, confirmed that groundbreaking for the Dangote East African Refinery in Lamu will take place on September 30, with land already secured. The plant is planned to exceed the Nigerian refinery scale and is projected to create about 60,000 jobs, with Ruto saying Kenya is removing administrative hurdles to keep the project on schedule.

title: Dangote, Ethiopia and Djibouti to build $660m fuel pipeline and storage project
body: Aliko Dangote, Ethiopia and Djibouti have agreed to develop a $660m petroleum pipeline and storage project linking Djibouti Damerjog port to a distribution facility at Dewele, Ethiopia, with about 400 million litres of storage and operations expected within 18 months. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said the pipeline would cut fuel transport time from Djibouti to Addis Ababa from five days to one, strengthening landlocked Ethiopia supply chain resilience.

title: Africa warned not to repeat the crude oil model with lithium and critical minerals
body: At a critical minerals session, World Energy Council Nigeria CEO Bala Wunti cautioned that Africa must not repeat with lithium, cobalt and rare earths the model of exporting raw crude while importing refined products, urging investment in processing capacity, bankable projects and local value addition. He cited the US $110/kg price floor for neodymium and praseodymium under the MP Materials agreement as an example of interventions that give investors commercial certainty.

title: Dangote Lamu refinery to include 1,000MW power plant, half for Kenya's grid
body: Aliko Dangote said the planned Lamu refinery in Kenya will generate about 1,000 megawatts of electricity, with roughly 500 megawatts potentially sold to the Kenyan government once the plant operates. He called the refinery the 'gate' to wider investment in Kenya, and the project is due to break ground on September 30. It is planned at 700,000 barrels per day with backing from the Africa Finance Corporation.

title: Uganda unveils $1.2 billion Roosevelt Africa Trail pipeline under US 'Trade Over Aid' plan
body: The United States named Uganda's Roosevelt Africa Trail the first project under its Trade Over Aid Deals framework, putting an indicative $1.2 billion investment pipeline before American financiers at a UN General Assembly week showcase. The corridor spans tourism, agriculture, technology and conservation from Lake Victoria through Murchison Falls to West Nile, including a proposed museum, smart monuments and a branded safari-coffee value chain. The figure is a pipeline of proposed projects, not committed financing — each still needs feasibility and due diligence.

title: Ghana's Mahama: AU chairmanship to push AfCFTA and mineral value addition
body: President John Mahama used his UN General Assembly address to signal that Ghana's incoming African Union chairmanship in January 2027 will champion continental integration, faster AfCFTA implementation and domestic processing of critical minerals. 'Critical mineral extraction must not replicate colonial-era exploitation,' he said, committing Africa to processing minerals at home and retaining resource value on the continent.

title: Ogun State and DP World sign MoUs for Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Economic Zone, over $7bn initial investment
body: Ogun State signed MoUs with DP World MEA FZE in Paris — witnessed by President Tinubu — for the Gateway Deep Seaport at Ogun Waterside and the 10,000-hectare Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone. The projects are projected to attract more than $7 billion in initial investment and over 50,000 direct jobs, with the port's planned 18-metre draft intended to relieve congestion at Lagos ports and serve AfCFTA trade.

title: AfCFTA digital trade rules could unlock Africa's $700bn digital economy by 2035
body: AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene said the Protocol on Digital Trade — covering digital identities, cross-border payments, data transfers, fintech and emerging technologies including AI — is meant to create a unified digital market across Africa's $3.4 trillion, 1.4-billion-person bloc. Africa's digital economy could generate more than $700 billion by 2035 if regulatory barriers to cross-border digital business are removed.

title: AfDB projects Central Africa growth rising to 3.8% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027
body: Launching its 2026 Regional Economic Outlook for Central Africa at the Bank of Central African States in Yaoundé, the African Development Bank projected regional growth rising from 3.6% in 2025 to 3.8% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027. The report estimates structural-transformation financing requirements of $42.9 billion per year by 2030 against a $35.6 billion annual financing gap.

title: Nigeria and US sign critical minerals investment framework on UNGA sidelines
body: Nigeria and the United States signed a minerals investment framework in New York, at Nigeria's Mission House during UNGA 81, aimed at facilitating private-sector investment across Nigeria's mining value chain. The $700 billion figure attached to the deal is Nigeria's own estimate of its undeveloped mineral potential - not a US investment pledge - and fact-checkers caution the framework contains no US payment. Nigeria ranks second globally in tantalum production and is positioning for lithium and rare-earth processing projects already underway.

title: Uganda unveils $1.2bn Roosevelt Africa Trail pipeline under US 'Trade Over Aid' plan
body: The US has named Uganda's Roosevelt Africa Trail the first project under its Trade Over Aid Deals framework, placing an indicative $1.2 billion investment pipeline before American financiers, announced at a showcase in New York on September 25. The pipeline spans tourism, coffee value-addition, infrastructure, agriculture and technology, and is not yet approved or disbursed - individual projects still face feasibility, due diligence and financing approvals. Kenya and South Sudan, part of the wider trail, are expected to develop separate national pipelines.

title: China-Africa report puts AI and digital trade at the centre of economic cooperation
body: A new report, 'China-Africa Economic and Trade Cooperation: Progress and Outlook 2026', unveiled at the Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, positions AI and digital trade as new growth drivers in China-Africa cooperation. The AU's permanent representative to China called for cooperation in cross-border e-commerce, interoperable payments, data governance, and linking Chinese digital trade parks with African special economic zones.
